The lane brief adds two constraints that shape execution: all changes stay in this detached worktree, and the parent owns GitHub writes, so I’ll leave issue labels/comments alone. I’m mapping the existing model and policy fixture interfaces now, including the exact campaign near misses for the approved rules.

The repository already has the needed building blocks: policies can bind exact callable identities through `resolved-call`, and taint/typestate can consume call-argument facts. I’ll keep this additive: test-only policy models plus reusable Python model artifacts where identity is missing, with no new RQL vocabulary or analyzer-store schema. The parent’s boundary leaves URL decomposition and external-call classification out of this lane.

The ExecPlan is in place and committed in the assigned worktree. One important constraint is now explicit: these are model-conformance fixtures, while release rule authoring remains outside this repo; I’m checking that exact call selectors can distinguish the campaign’s fake APIs and safe arguments before choosing the smallest model representation.

I’ve added the first current-checkout policy fixture: it requires the resolved `flask.Flask.run` identity, its `debug` formal argument, and literal `True`, with `Other.run(True)` and `debug=False` as controls. I’m running this focused test now; if the existing Python resolver cannot prove that identity, I’ll use the failure to pin the missing capability rather than weaken the selector.

The first focused run is still compiling the workspace with Python enabled; this worktree had no reusable test binary. Compilation has reached the analysis crate, and the test is queued behind that build.

The build is waiting on `brokk-bifrost-analysis`, with other lanes compiling concurrently; disk space is ample and no test failure has surfaced. I’m letting nextest’s normal build proceed without changing the shared Cargo target or concurrency settings.

The compile has advanced past the Rust dependency graph into jemalloc linking, but the first build is still slow under parallel lane activity. The policy and test sources are ready; once the binary is built, the next run should reuse it.

I’m continuing the assigned implementation in the models-config worktree. The first focused policy run is still building; I’ll use its result to settle the query shape, then complete the remaining API and web fixtures, run the lane gate, commit, and hand back the evidence.

The prototype’s key constraint is now clear: a local mock class can prove the RQL shape, but it would not establish the requested library identity. I’m checking how Python semantic packs bind external declarations and value roles so the fixtures exercise reviewed `flask`, `paramiko`, `requests`, and `ssl` identities, with the cookie/CSRF and web-source slices using the same shipped model path.

The lane now has exact-call policy fixtures for the four direct API rules, cookie and CSRF configuration cases, plus an end-to-end taint fixture joining Flask/Django request reads to response writes. The fixtures include the campaign controls (wrong receiver, safe values, non-sensitive cookie names, and non-reaching sources). I’m moving into validation now; the initial Cargo build is still waiting on shared compilation work, so I’m first checking formatting and plan consistency while it runs.
